name: PT Dharma Satya Nusantara Tbk

frontmatter.title: Dharma Satya Nusantara: a planter priced for a palm-price fall, and a service fee that sets its wedge
frontmatter.summary: Two 13 November policy items: DSI's palm export platform starts on 1 January 2027 with a provisional single-digit dollar fee, and GAPKI raised its 2027 El Nino loss to up to 3,000 kt [S20, S17]. The fee is carried in the base as a partial pass-through and sized in the bear; the B50 review is carried in the price deck both ways; and the World Bank's Outlook supports the deck [S22, S19]. BUY at Rp2,381, 89.1% from Rp1,285.
thesis: The DCF enterprise value of IDR28.98tn is a first-forecast-year multiple: on next year's EBITDA of IDR4,972bn it sits above the 5.3x the cross-check applies and further above the 4.1x the market pays, so the value rests on the cash-flow path rather than on a multiple [S3, S4].

At Rp1,285 the market discounts a palm price of US$1,095/t, below spot, below the deck and below the World Bank's next-year forecast of US$1,256.0, so the disagreement is about the recovery, not about today [S0, S8, S22].

Volume is revised down from the printed plan to 625.0 kt, because the nine-month outturn of 451 kt is already below last year, and then takes the company's own fruit decline into next year at 595.0 kt; the pro-rata slice of the national loss stays in the bear [S4, S5, S17, F34, F35, F86].

The supply backdrop has tightened: GAPKI now puts the El Nino loss at up to 3,000 kt, the worst in the year the deck prices the peak, and the World Bank sees prices rising next year on that same shortfall [S17, S22, F86].

The levy-plus-freight wedge, not a proportional haircut, sets the realised price, and the DSI fee is an order of magnitude smaller than the charge it sits inside, so it is a partial pass-through in the base and at the top of its range in the bear; the index de-rating is sized separately [S6, F36, S11, S19].

blocks.text: **What changed, and why.** Two 13 November policy items. The DSI fee is carried as a modelled input, a partial pass-through at 0.2% of palm revenue from FY2027E; only the B50 outcome is not a separate input, and it is carried in the price deck both ways. DSI said it will publish its service tariff in December and that the provisional calculation is a single-digit dollar amount, the first quantification of the fee the palm export channel will charge from 1 January 2027; GAPKI's chairman put DSI as a fourth layer on top of the export levy, the export tax and the domestic-market obligation, and warned that a fee at the top of that range would reach the domestic price calculation [S19, S20]. Separately, the energy ministry said it will evaluate the 2027 B50 mandate the following week, so the domestic demand pillar is under review rather than settled [S21]. The bear carries the top of the fee range in its wedge leg, and the World Bank's October Outlook is the named public series the deck and terminal are checked against [S19, S20, S21, S22]. The larger model change is volume: FY2026E is cut to 625.0 kt from the company's printed one-per-cent growth plan, and FY2027E to 595.0 kt, on the nine-month outturn and the company's own fruit decline [F34, F35, F60, F86]. Sections three, four and five carry the revision, and the twelve-month value moves from the two thousand four hundred and thirty-eight rupiah published on 12 November to Rp2,381.

**The two policy items, sized.** The fee reaches a domestic seller through the parity price, not as a charge on its own sales: DSNG's palm line is domestic, so the base carries a partial pass-through at 0.2% of palm revenue and the bear carries the top of the single-digit range inside its wedge leg [S19, S20, S6, F36, F61]. The B50 review is a demand question for the deck: confirmation validates the deck price the base already carries and a delay takes that support off it, and the scenario set moves the deck both ways [S21, S6, S8]. The DHE SDA conversion relaxation is checked and immaterial to cash flow: exports are IDR977.3bn of wood products and shells in nine months against group revenue of IDR9,109.8bn, and the move changes the timing of rupiah conversion, not price or cost, so it is not in the base or the bull [S9, S10, F72, F75, F76, F31].

The view is BUY at a twelve-month value of Rp2,381, a total return of 89.1% from Rp1,285, of which 85.3% is price appreciation and the balance the next-twelve-month dividend. The World Bank's October Outlook forecasts the palm price rising next year on the same El Nino shortfall, and its 2028 print sits within a few dollars of our terminal marker while its later prints are lower, so the public through-cycle view supports the deck the market refuses to pay for [S22, F91, F92, F94, F95].

DSNG is an integrated oil-palm producer: 111,900 ha of planted area, split between nucleus estates it owns and plasma blocks it develops for smallholders, with mills in East, Central and West Kalimantan; a wood-products business making engineered flooring and panels in Central Java; and a renewables business exporting palm-kernel shells and wood pellets to Japan and Korea [S4, S7, F38]. Last year CPO production reached 631 kt, sales 629 kt and the extraction rate 23.3% [S3, F1, F23, F26].

Almost all of the value is palm: the segment took 88.0% of nine-month revenue of 9,110 IDR bn, and the export line is almost entirely the other two segments [S2, F54, F31]. Strategy is unglamorous: replant older blocks, finish the plasma programme, delever, add small downstream projects such as a bio-CNG plant using mill effluent [S4, S7]. There is no large acquisition, so the capital question is whether dividend and replanting can both be funded from operating cash flow, and last year they were [S3, F50]. Control sits with the Triputra and Oetomo families, holding 30.6% and 29.2%, with an Oetomo family member as president director; the estate is held through operating subsidiaries and a stake in an associated estate in East Kalimantan, with a small non-controlling interest, no dual-class structure and no share pledge [S2, S4, F55, F56].

The palm price is the largest driver. The in-house CPO driver deck (d.agri.cpo) runs CPO to US$1,135/t this year and US$1,240/t next, then fades to US$1,150/t long-run. The deck is built on the World Bank Pink Sheet, whose annual averages are US$886/t in 2023, US$963/t in 2024 and US$1,007/t in 2025 [S16], and on the Bursa FCPO forward strip. The World Bank's October Outlook, the named public series we check the deck against, forecasts the price rising next year and falling in the year after on an El Nino-curbed supply: its 2028 print of US$1,144.0 is within a few dollars of the deck's long-run marker, but its later prints of US$1,089.0 and US$1,096.0 are lower, so the marker carries a premium of about a fifth to the 2023-25 realised average, which the deck basis attributes to the structural biodiesel bid and recurring El Nino risk [S22, F91, F92, F94, F95]. Supply has tightened again: at IPOC on 12 November GAPKI's chairman put the El Nino loss at up to 3,000 kt, heaviest in 2027, above the 2,200 kt the deck's next-year price rested on [S17, S8, F86, F37]. DSNG's own trough is earlier: nine-month fruit output 1,500 kt, CPO 451 kt [S5, F35, F34].

Policy is set monthly. The Ministry of Trade sets a reference price and derives the export duty and levy from it; for November the reference price is US$979/t and the combined charge US$246/t, down a fifth on October's US$308/t [S6, F36, F48, F77]. Because the charge is a dollar amount per tonne, not a proportional cut, the wedge shrinks as a ratio when the benchmark rises, which is what our realisation assumption carries [S6, S3]. The biodiesel mandate is the other pillar: the government confirmed the B50 blend, and palm use for biodiesel was 1,350 kt in August while exports rose and stocks fell [S6, F49]. It is not settled for next year: the energy ministry said on 13 November that it will evaluate the 2027 mandate the following week, and that mandate is the demand pillar the deck price rests on [S21, S8]. DSI itself says the tariff will be published in December and describes the provisional calculation as a single-digit dollar amount, and GAPKI counts DSI as a fourth cost layer after the levy, the tax and the domestic-market obligation [S20, S19].

Competitive position is cost and certification, not share. DSNG is a small producer and a price taker, but its cash cost per tonne is set by its own estate and mill efficiency, with mills close to the fruit and an extraction rate of 23.3% [S4, F26]. It has no pricing power, which is why it is valued on a through-cycle price rather than a multiple of one year's earnings [S3]. The market backdrop is a separate risk: MSCI is consulting on reclassifying Indonesia to standalone, which for a domestic mid-cap with a 33.1% free float is a de-rating with nothing to do with palm oil [S11, S0].

FY2026E against the company plan. The 2025 annual report prints its own 2026 projection as revenue flat and pre-tax profit up about a twentieth [S4]. We carry volume at 625.0 kt, below the printed plan because the nine-month outturn of 451 kt is already below the prior year, so a full-year target now requires a fourth quarter matching last year's rather than beating it; plan achievement is the bull, not the base [F34, F60]. From FY2027E the model is below the plan on volume because the heaviest El Nino impact falls beyond it [F86].

The last audited year is the anchor. Revenue was 12,315 IDR bn, cost of revenue 8,465 IDR bn and gross profit IDR3,850.0bn [S3, F5, F7]. Cost of revenue carries D&A of 974 IDR bn, which the data pack understated by an order of magnitude, so depreciation is restated to the audited note; on that basis EBITDA was IDR3,814.6bn at a margin of 31.0% [S3, F9]. Every EBITDA here is operating EBITDA: audited operating profit plus fixed-asset and right-of-use depreciation plus bearer-plant and intangible amortisation, the associate excluded, no add-back of the impairment and no deduction of the biological gain, a fraction of a per cent above operating profit of IDR2,829.4bn plus D&A of IDR973.7bn [S3, F65, F9].

The cash cost of a tonne of CPO is about IDR8.0m, well below the US$886.0 trough of the last three audited years and a fraction of the November reference price of US$979/t, so the estate is cash-positive at any observed price; we cannot source a global cost curve that carries DSNG, so we state the comparison rather than claim a quartile [S16, F79, F48]. The plantation is amortised over 20 years, and planted area of 111,900 ha over that life needs about five and a half thousand hectares of replanting a year, so the model carries capex of IDR1,046.8bn, above D&A of IDR992.2bn: replacement on the filing's own productive life, not a haircut [S3, F85, F38, F9]. Costs are held at the last actual in real terms, inflated at the long-run rupiah anchor, and the plasma outlay is excluded because collections in the same investing section reimburse it [S0, S3, F11].

Next year the deck does the work on price. The realisation ratio is not held flat: the accounts show a dollar wedge between benchmark and realised price that behaves like a levy-plus-freight amount, so we hold the wedge and let the ratio rise with the benchmark [S2, S6, F36, F48]. Revenue reaches IDR13,676.5bn and EBITDA IDR4,972.0bn [S0, S3]. Volume takes the company's own trough: 595.0 kt against the 625.0 kt base, about four per cent lower, the same rate as the nine-month fall in fruit output to 1,500 kt kt [S5, F35]. That is the most likely path: GAPKI's loss is weighted to 2027 [S17, F86], and the World Bank's own forecast prices that same shortfall [S22, F91]. The pro-rata slice of the upper bound stays the bear's volume leg, and the recovery starts in FY2028E at 610.0 kt [S17, F86, F38].

The non-palm line is built, not escalated. Last year's non-CPO revenue of IDR3,216.9bn is palm kernel and kernel oil, wood and renewables [S3, F29]. Kernel scales with CPO volume; wood and renewables are held at the nine-month run-rate annualised, below last year because wood revenue and its margin fell, and no wood recovery is assumed, so a DHE-driven recovery is upside [S2, S9, S10]. The blended gross margin of 20.0% is a blend: kernel earns the palm-segment margin, wood a fifth of it [S3, S2].

The balance sheet is sound: forecast net debt at the year end of IDR2,447.2bn is 0.6x this year's EBITDA, about two-thirds, against attributable equity of 11,481 IDR bn [S2, S3, F15], and the dividend at a payout of 27.1% and the replanting inside own capex are the claims on cash [S3, F21]. Accruals are negative in both fiscal years and in the nine months, and operating cash flow has exceeded net profit in every period [S3, S2, F13, F50, F41]. We can source the 2013 listing but not the IDX board or notation status, so we assert none; the one optics-class item is the land revaluation surplus of 2,585 IDR bn, which inflates book equity but not cash flow [S4, S3, F57].

**Method note.** We value DSNG on a DCF as the primary method, with an EV/EBITDA and a P/BV cross-check. The DCF carries the controlling weight because the company is a price-taking commodity producer whose value is a long stream of cash flows at a through-cycle price, while a multiple capitalises whatever point of the cycle its year sits on [S3, S4]. The cross-checks blend a filtered six-name palm peer set with our own five-year means, which gives 5.3x EV/EBITDA and 0.9x P/BV. The market comparison is not like-for-like on the book leg: the 1.1x is on reported book, which includes the land revaluation surplus, while our P/BV is applied to pre-revaluation book; on the same pre-revaluation book of IDR9,862.6bn the market pays about half again the multiple the leg applies at Rp1,285 [S0, S2, S3, F62, F63].

The cost of capital comes from the house macro deck and the industry configuration: a rupiah risk-free rate of 7.4% less the default spread of 1.6%, plus a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2% and a country risk premium of 2.5%, on an unlevered beta of 0.80 relevered to 0.95 [S4]. That gives a cost of equity of 12.2% and a WACC of 11.3% at a debt weight of 19.3% [S4]. Two debt rates do two jobs: the WACC prices debt at the marginal 9.4%, while the model's 7.9% is the effective cost on opening debt, FY2025 finance costs of IDR452bn over that base [S3, S4, F18]. Terminal growth of 2.5% is the house macro deck's long-run rupiah inflation (macro: inflation_idr_lt).

The DCF produces Rp2,618 per share, with the terminal value at 45.8% of enterprise value and free cash flow rising from IDR1,790.9bn this year to IDR2,479.8bn in five years [S0, S3]. The terminal marker of US$1,150/t is a premium to the observed path, and we state it as such: it is about a fifth above the 2023-25 realised average, about half a per cent above the World Bank's 2028 print of US$1,144.0, and about a twentieth above its lower 2029 and 2030 prints of US$1,089.0 and US$1,096.0. The premium is the deck's own basis, not an add-on: the anchor is the 2026 tape plus the structural biodiesel bid (Indonesia B40 toward B50, Malaysia B20) and recurring El Nino supply risk, and it escalates with the rupiah cost base rather than US inflation because palm is priced in dollars and costed in rupiah. The terminal stays on the engine deck path; the public series is a check, not the input [S22, F91, F92, F94, F95]. The perpetuity also rests on tenure, not just price: the HGU titles run up to 33 years and expire between 2030 and 2058, and we assume they are renewed on expiry as Indonesian HGU rights customarily are, with the estate replanted on its 20-year productive life, so the terminal value is a continuing estate rather than a wasting concession [S4, F93, F85].

The DCF enterprise value is IDR28,983bn. Against this year's operating EBITDA of IDR3,925bn that is well above both the 5.3x the cross-check applies and the 4.1x the market pays, and on next year's EBITDA of IDR4,972bn the same enterprise value sits above the cross-check's multiple, not below it: the cross-check capitalises last year's EBITDA while the DCF capitalises the recovery [S3, S4]. The market's 4.1x is in line with the liquid palm peer median, so the market is discounting the cash-flow path, and that is the disagreement [S3, S8].

The two cross-checks sit below: EV/EBITDA applies 5.3x to last year's operating EBITDA of 3,814.6 for Rp1,785, -31.8% against the primary [S3]. That is a below-cycle year: realised CPO of US$879.7 sat under the deck's US$1,135/t, so the leg capitalises a trough and is conservative on that count rather than a mid-cycle value [S3, F3]. P/BV applies 0.9x to pre-revaluation book equity of IDR9,862.6bn, attributable equity less the land surplus of IDR2,585.1bn, for Rp867, -66.9% against the primary, on the same pre-revaluation base as the market comparison in the method note [S0, S2, F62, F63]. Pre-revaluation book is what the earnings-quality card requires: the surplus never reaches cash flow, and a book multiple cannot see the cash between replantings, so the leg is a floor [S3, F57, S4]. The associate is in the bridge at book, IDR1,578.9bn, about nine times last year's share of its profit of IDR168.4bn, so not an obviously cheap mark [S2, F44, F52].

The reverse DCF is the cleanest statement of the mispricing. At Rp1,285 the market discounts a palm price of US$1,095/t on our cost base and cost of capital, 88.3% of the deck's next-year level [S0, S3]. Against spot of US$1,180/t and the World Bank's next-year forecast of US$1,256.0, the market assumes not that the price stays but that it falls and then does not recover; the World Bank's public view and the GAPKI loss both say the opposite, so the disagreement is the recovery [S8, F37, S22, S17].

The sensitivity table shows what matters. A palm-price move passes almost straight to the margin, a volume move carries a cost because the estate's costs are largely fixed, and the exchange rate acts like a price move because revenue is dollar-denominated and cost is rupiah [S0, S3]. The grid holds the long-run deck flat in nominal terms while the base escalates it, so every cell reads low against a like-for-like re-run; read it for the ordering of risk, and the four-fifths column is the through-cycle case for a sceptic [S0, S16].

Two prior kills on this name are restated rather than buried. The July 2026 valuation kill rested on a through-cycle NAV that did not support the exit level then planned; this work rests on the audited FY2025 notes and the nine-month 2026 LK, and the restated D&A and the segment revenue base move that anchor [S3, S2]. The August 2026 liquidity kill stands: at the disclosed ADTV a house-size position is many sessions of turnover [S0].

The DHE SDA conversion relaxation, from the present cap to full conversion, is checked and immaterial to cash flow: the export line is IDR977.3bn in nine months against group revenue of IDR9,109.8bn, the wood products in it are manufactured goods rather than a raw natural-resource commodity, and the move changes only the timing of rupiah conversion [S9, S10, F72, F75, F76, F31].

The bear cuts the palm price a fifth, trims volume a twentieth, strengthens the rupiah a tenth and widens the levy-plus-freight wedge a tenth, and values the shares at Rp647, below the current price [S3, S6]. The B50 outcome is carried in the price leg, not as a separate haircut: a delay removes the domestic absorption that supports the benchmark, and the same leg supports the bull when confirmation validates the deck the base already carries [S21, S8]. The DSI fee sits in the wedge leg: at the top of the single-digit range it is an order of magnitude smaller than the charge it adds to [S19, F36]. The base case is Rp2,360 and the bull Rp4,158, at 25%, 50% and 25%; the bull moves the same four drivers the other way, so the spread is the operating leverage of the estate [S3, S8].

We sized the two risks a commodity scenario cannot carry. A levy a fifth wider than the November charge takes the value to about nine tenths of Rp2,381 and the return to five sixths of the base; it is the largest policy number in the file, and why the wedge rather than the benchmark is the variable to watch [S6, F36, F48]. The index de-rating is a cost-of-equity event: a one-point premium takes the value to about nineteen twentieths of Rp2,381 [S11, S0].

The operating risks are ordinary. A sustained fall in the dollar price hits revenue directly and widens the domestic discount if the levy is not cut in step [S6, S8]. El Nino has already cut fruit production [S5, F35], and GAPKI now puts the industry loss at up to 3,000 kt with the worst ahead in 2027, so a second dry year pushes the recovery out and raises unit cost [S17, F86]. At Rp18,140/USD the rupiah is close to its weakest on record, helping revenue and raising the rupiah cost of imported inputs [S6, F47]. Replanting reduces the mature area before it increases it, and GAPKI's own remedy takes years to reach yield [S4, S17].

Liquidity is adequate but not deep: average daily traded value of IDR7.3bn, a free float of 33.1% and a twelve-month range of Rp1,075.0 to Rp1,860.0, so a large holder would need patience [S0]. The signposts are specific: an MSCI decision that makes reclassification likely [S11]; a published DSI tariff or range above current invoices, a levy increase, or a second quarter of falling fruit production [S15, S6, S5]; and on the other side a confirmed national decline with a rising reference price, and monthly crop data showing the 3,000 kt upper bound is not being reached [S17, S8, F86].

DSNG is controlled by two families: the Triputra interests hold 30.6% and the Oetomo interests 29.2%, with a further block held by an investment company, and the president director is an Oetomo, so control and management are the same people [S4, S3, F55, F56]. The public holds 33.1%, comfortably above the minimum [S0, S4].

The audit is clean: the Indonesian KPMG member firm, unmodified, with independent commissioners alongside executive directors, no dual-class structure and no share pledge — the security is over bearer plants, inventory and receivables [S4, S3, S2, F82]. Related-party dealings are modest: trade payables to related parties were 2.0 IDR bn at the end of September against third-party payables many times larger, and the associated estate is a related party because the company holds a stake in it; a loan to that associate was repaid in full, so there is no related-party financing exposure [S2, S3, F53, F44, F52].

The dividend record is consistent: Rp47.0/share declared for the last financial year and Rp24.0/share the year before, a payout of about 27.1% of earnings, covered by free cash flow and inside the stated policy band [S3, F21, F22, F50]. At through-cycle free cash flow the equity generates an FCFE yield of 11.5% against a dividend yield of 3.8%, so the net-cash build by FY2028 is reachable as a higher payout rather than stranded [S3, F21].

On ESG the certification stack is the strongest part: every mill is ISPO certified, most are RSPO certified, and the nucleus estates are certified at a high share under both [S4]. The plasma programme gives smallholders a stake and reduces land-conflict risk, and the bio-CNG plant captures mill effluent [S4, F38]. The remaining exposures are industry-standard: European deforestation rules, weak flooring demand, and land and labour risk across 19,037 employees [S4, S7].

The nearest is the DSI tariff, to be published in December before the 1 January 2027 start: its provisional description of a single-digit dollar fee makes the earlier illustration of one per cent of export value an upper bound rather than a base, and we will size the published number against the realisation assumption [S15, S13, S20, F36]. The second is the ESDM evaluation of the 2027 B50 mandate, the following week, which is the demand case for the deck price in the base and both scenarios [S21]. The third is the monthly policy reset: the November package cut the charge to US$246/t while the reference price fell to US$979/t, so parity was flat and the December print matters for the fourth quarter [S6, F36, F48]. The fourth is the fourth-quarter production report, which shows whether the El Nino decline in Kalimantan has turned [S5, F35]. The fifth is the full-year result and the dividend, on our forecast Rp49 over the next twelve months [S3, F21]. The sixth is the GAPKI data flow, testing whether the 2027 loss reaches the 3,000 kt upper bound or settles nearer the 2,200 kt the deck was built on [S17, S8].

Between updates the monitoring set is the MSCI consultation, the December DSI tariff and price range, the ESDM evaluation, the monthly reference price and levy, quarterly fruit and CPO volumes, the realised price per tonne implied by segment revenue, and unit cash cost and net debt [S11, S15, S20, S21, S6, S5, S2, S3].

bear.narrative: El Nino persists into 2027 with damaged trees needing more than a season of recovery, and the volume leg takes a pro-rata slice of GAPKI's upper-bound national loss on top of the base cut; the price leg is a fifth off the deck, and that leg carries the B50 outcome as a demand shock — ESDM delaying or diluting the 2027 mandate removes the domestic absorption that supports the benchmark rather than repricing it, so the demand shock is a lower deck, not a separate price haircut; the rupiah strengthens a tenth; the wedge leg widens the levy-plus-freight wedge a tenth, and that wedge leg is where the DSI fee sits — at the top of the single-digit range the fee is an order of magnitude smaller than the charge it adds to, so the wedge leg contains the fee several times over and leaves the levy widening to fill the rest. The MSCI standalone risk is a de-rating sized separately, not stacked here.

bull.narrative: A stronger 2027 supply deficit after GAPKI raised its loss estimate to up to 3.0m tonnes with the worst in 2027, above the 2.2m tonnes the deck was built on, lifts CPO a fifth above the deck, and that same deck leg carries the B50 outcome the other way — ESDM confirming the 2027 mandate next week validates the domestic demand pillar the deck already assumes, so the confirmation is not a separate upside on top of the deck but the demand case for the deck price; El Nino recovery plus plasma maturities add 5% to volume; the rupiah weakens a tenth; and the wedge leg narrows a tenth, with the DSI tariff landing at the bottom of the single-digit range and its small parity effect inside that same leg — the fee at the low end barely registers against the November charge. The four drivers are the same four the bear moves, in the opposite direction, so the spread in the values is the operating leverage of the estate, not a different set of assumptions.

assumptions.label: CPO sales volume plan adjusted for nine-month trend
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is revised down from company's +1% plan of 637 kt to 625 kt, reflecting nine-month CPO production of 451 kt [F34] that is 1.5% below prior year run-rate. A full-year target now requires Q4 of 174 kt, matching last year's Q4 exactly, which is plausible but eliminates upside; the company's original plan implied 186 kt Q4 (637 - 451). The risk of missing even this lowered base resides in bear volume shock. FY2027E is cut further to 595 kt (-4.8% year-on-year), reflecting both DSNG's nine-month FFB decline of 4.3% [F35] and GAPKI's national forecast of heaviest El Nino impact in 2027 [F86, S17]. Recovery begins in FY2028E at 610 kt, returning to 635 kt by FY2030E, below original 655 kt target due to cumulative effect of drought and delayed replanting cycle. The pro-rata slice of national loss upper-bound remains in bear scenario as a shock stacked on these reduced levels. Sources updated to reflect actual vs plan gap [F34, F35, S5].

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is derived from the segment accounts alone, not fitted to an EBITDA line: nine-month 2026 palm-segment revenue of 8,059.213 [S2] on 451 kt of CPO production [F34] is Rp17.87m per tonne; CPO sales track production (FY2025 sales 628.737 kt against production 631.046 kt, 99.6% [F1, F23]), so the production denominator is immaterial. Stripping by-products at the FY2025 per-tonne value (1,748.322 of non-CPO palm revenue on 628.737 kt = Rp2.781m [F5, F29]) leaves Rp15.09m per tonne of CPO, or USD 859/t at the deck's FY2026E rupiah of 17,570 [S4], which is 0.757 of the deck's USD 1,135/t benchmark. The ratio is not a haircut fitted to a line: it is the observed dollar wedge, and the wedge is the primitive. FY2025A realised USD 879.74/t against a USD 1,007/t benchmark is a wedge of USD 127/t [F3, F81]; the November 2026 reference price of 978.90 less the levy-plus-duty charge of 246.36 gives net export parity of 732.54 [F48, F36]. The charge does not scale proportionally with the benchmark, and the basis now separates the two legs: the November 246.36 is a specific bea keluar export duty of 124.00 (178.00 in October, set by the reference-price band) plus an ad valorem levy of 122.36, which is 12.5% of the 978.90 reference [F36, S6]. Scaling the whole charge by the benchmark would give USD 285.7/t and a ratio of 0.748, but that is the wrong arithmetic; holding the specific duty and scaling only the levy gives 265.9/t before freight, so the observed wedge of about 276 on the benchmark (the charge plus about 30 of freight) sits inside the range the two-leg split allows and is calibrated on the nine-month actual, not on a scaled forecast. The band step is the risk: if the reference crosses 1,000 the duty returns to the October level and the wedge widens toward 320, cutting the ratio toward 0.72; that sensitivity is carried in the bear's widened wedge leg, not in the base. The wedge nearly doubled because the charge rose to the November level, so the ratio falls from 0.874 to 0.757; it is a sourced policy wedge, not a default haircut [S6, F36, F77]. From FY2027E the ratio is derived from the dollar wedge instead of being held flat: the wedge is a levy-plus-freight amount, not a proportional haircut, so the ratio rises as the benchmark rises. Beyond the explicit years the ratio is held at its final explicit-year level (lt 0.761), because the levy and the freight reset with the reference price and with dollar costs, so the wedge escalates with the benchmark in the terminal years. REVISED after red team C20: the calibration gap is the direct consequence of this structure and is reconciled line by line in qc_justifications.calibration.ebitda. The DSI single-intermediary export channel from 1 January 2027 is carried as a partial pass-through in a.royalty_rate from FY2027E, not in this ratio: DSNG exports no CPO [F61], so the fee reaches it only through the domestic price its refinery buyers pay [S12, S13, S15, S19, S20].

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: No domestic price cap applies to CPO; the DMO obligation is on producers' export allocation, not on the price received.

assumptions.label: Cost-intensity factor (bcm per tonne equivalent)
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 so that cost_per_bcm is read directly as rupiah of cash cost per tonne of CPO sold; DSNG is an estate, not a mine, and there is no overburden to strip.

assumptions.label: Cash cost per tonne of CPO (IDR)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 cash COGS = cost of revenue 8,464.728 less D&A 973.744 = 7,490.984 [F7, F9]; less the cost of the 3,216.888 of non-CPO revenue at a 20% gross margin = 2,573.510, leaving 4,917.474 for 628.737 kt = Rp7.821m per tonne [F1, F29]. Escalated at the 2.5% long-run rupiah inflation in the macro deck.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of cash cost
assumptions.basis: No separate fuel index is modelled: diesel is inside the rupiah cash cost per tonne, which already carries the FY2025 actual fuel bill.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Zero: haulage, milling and overhead are already inside the audited cost of revenue from which cost_per_bcm is derived, so adding a second per-tonne charge would double-count.

assumptions.label: DSI service fee partial pass-through to the domestic price (proxy as royalty)
assumptions.basis: Zero in FY2026E (the channel starts 1 Jan 2027). From FY2027E the base carries a partial pass-through of the DSI service fee, not the whole fee: DSNG sells its CPO line wholly into the domestic market with nil export sales [F61], so the fee, charged on CPO exports through the DSI platform, reaches it only through the domestic parity price, and the pass-through is not the full fee because the domestic price is negotiated against, not set by, export parity [S12, S13, S19, S20]. DSI describes the provisional calculation as a single-digit dollar amount with the tariff published in December 2026 [S20]; GAPKI puts the top of that range at nine dollars a tonne and warns it would reach the domestic price calculation [S19]. On a mid-range fee at the deck benchmark, a half pass-through is about two tenths of a per cent of the CPO revenue, so the base carries 0.2% from FY2027E [S4]. The top-of-range fee is carried in the bear through the widened realisation (wedge) leg rather than a separate shock, because a single-digit dollar fee is an order of magnitude smaller than the levy-plus-freight wedge it sits inside [S6, F36].

assumptions.label: Other revenue (PK, PKO, wood products, renewables)
assumptions.basis: Built in two parts, not held flat by default. FY2025 non-CPO revenue 3,216.888 = PK/PKO 1,748.322 + wood 1,242.325 + renewables 226.241 [F5, F29, S3]. The PK/PKO line is a palm by-product and scales with CPO volume, so FY2026E carries it at the revised base volume, not the pre-revision plan: 1,748.322 x 625/631 = 1,732.0. (The earlier 1,764.6 used the 637 kt plan and was inconsistent with the volume cut; the 32.6bn difference is about one per cent of other revenue.) Wood and renewables are held at the nine-month run-rate annualised, 1,050.596 x 4/3 = 1,400.8, which is below the FY2025 level of 1,468.566 because wood revenue fell to 897.400 in the nine months and its gross margin to 5.5% while renewables held at 23.0% [S2]; that is the segment accounts, not a default haircut, and no wood or flooring recovery is assumed in the base, so a DHE-driven or flooring recovery is upside. FY2026E total 3,132.8, escalated at the 2.5% long-run rupiah inflation thereafter.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: 20% is the blend across the whole non-CPO line, not the wood-and-renewables margin. FY2025: palm segment revenue 10,846.146 and gross profit 3,660.509, wood 1,242.325 and 138.887 (11.2%), renewables 226.241 and 50.588 (22.4%) [S3]. The non-CPO line is PK/PKO 1,748.322 plus wood and renewables 1,468.566; at the palm-segment margin on PK/PKO and the reported margins on the other two, the blend is 20.0% and reconciles the group gross profit of 3,849.984 [S3]. Nine-month 2026: palm 8,059.213 and 2,826.156 (35.1%), wood 897.400 and 49.676 (5.5%), renewables 153.196 and 35.212 (23.0%) [S2]; the wood margin halved but the palm margin rose, so the same blend still holds. The red team's 8.1% is the wood-plus-renewables subset only, 1,050.596 of 9,109.809 revenue.

assumptions.label: D&A per tonne (IDR)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 total D&A 973.744 [F9] over 628.737 kt of CPO sold [F1] = Rp1.549m per tonne; escalated at 2.5% rupiah inflation. The pack's Rp65.922bn D&A line is not a D&A figure and is restated to the audited note.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per tonne (IDR)
assumptions.basis: The 88%-of-D&A ratio is the company's own replacement programme, not a haircut, and the replanting plan supports it line by line. FY2025 own capex 856.267 = fixed-asset additions 648.177 + capitalised plantation cost 208.090 [F11] over 628.737 kt [F1] = Rp1.362m per tonne. Split against the D&A components [F9]: fixed-asset additions 648.177 against fixed-asset depreciation 692.004 is 94%, and capitalised plantation 208.090 against bearer-plant and intangible amortisation of about 265.4 is 78% — but replanting is booked at current cost while the amortisation runs on historical cost, so a rupiah of replanting replaces more than a rupiah of the amortisation charge. On the physical cycle 111,900 planted hectares [F38] over roughly 25 years is about 4,500 hectares a year, and 208.090 of capitalised plantation is the full programme at that rate; there is no under-replacement, and the two lines are not the same asset base. Held at the last actual in real terms and escalated at the 2.5% long-run rupiah inflation (macro deck inflation_idr_lt, the BI target midpoint [S4]). The plasma outlay of 943.660 is excluded because the 1,019.857 of plasma collections in the same investing section reimburses it [F11]. REVISED after red team C7: the physical cycle is now the filings own 20-year productive life [F85, S3], not 25: 111,900 planted ha / 20 = 5,595 ha a year against the 4,500 the capex line funded, so sustaining capex rises 20% to Rp1.675m per tonne (the FY2025 actual 1.362m x 1.23), escalated at 2.5% [S3, S4].

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Zero: no separately disclosed expansion project is funded in the plan; the company's 2026 budget is maintenance and replanting, which sits in capex_unit.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital 1,144.975 / revenue 12,314.712 = 9.3%; the three-year average of 11.5% is inflated by the FY2022 inventory build. REVISED after red team C8: the three-year mean 11.5% is used, not the last actual, because a single-year low against a rising palm-price book is not a better forward guide and the low end was worth about Rp280bn of value.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 tax 670.747 / pre-tax profit 2,499.545 = 26.8%, held flat; the group has no material deferred-tax asset to run down.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance costs 452.485 [F18] / opening debt 5,733.094 = 7.9%; the 2020 sustainability bond of 181.924 was repaid during FY2025 (bonds payable nil at 31-Dec-2025, 181.924 at 31-Dec-2024, and 181.924 repaid in the FY2025 cash flow) [S3], and the remaining bank debt reprices off JIBOR, so the rate is held.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance income 12.552 [F19] / opening cash 557.023 = 2.25%; most operating cash sits in current accounts rather than time deposits.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero: debt fell from 5,733.094 to 4,105.200 in FY2025 and to 3,247.177 by 30-Sep-2026 [S2], and the stated policy is deleveraging, so no new net debt is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: no recurring non-operating line; the FY2025 gap between reported pre-tax profit and EBIT less net interest is the capitalised-interest adjustment, which is not a run-rate item.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero: the non-controlling interest is Rp139.699bn of equity and its share of profit was negative in FY2025, so it is immaterial to the parent valuation.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 DPS of Rp47 [F21] on EPS of Rp173.63 (profit 1,840.490 [F13] over 10,599.8424m shares [F20]) = 27.1%, inside the stated 25-30% policy band.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: 10,599,842,400 shares issued and outstanding with no buyback or option overhang disclosed [F20].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 2.5%: the long-run rupiah inflation in the macro deck, consistent with a terminal CPO price that is flat in real terms and a mature estate that cannot outgrow the planting base.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 SG&A and other opex 1,009.092 / revenue 12,314.712 = 8.19%; the three-year average of 8.96% is lifted by the FY2022-23 cost base. REVISED after red team C8: the three-year mean 8.96% is used; the last-actual 8.19% sat at the value-raising end of the disclosed range with no source for a structural saving.

challenges.challenge: Volume growth +1% for FY2026E uses company plan, but nine-month FFB production already down -4.3% and CPO -1.5% [F35, F34]; plan achievement requires heroic Q4, yet bear volume shock only 5%. Missing explicit downside risk to plan.
challenges.answer: FY2026E volume cut from the +1% plan to a figure below it, matching the nine-month FFB -4.3% run-rate [F34]; plan achievement moved to the bull. Volume shock kept at 0.95x in both scenarios.

challenges.challenge: Calibration gap -22% (EBITDA 2,976 vs 3,815) indicates FY2026E realisation (0.757) and rupiah (17,570) not reproducing last actual; justification says forward rates used, but MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE requires FY+1 at last-year prices.
challenges.answer: Line-by-line reconciliation added to qc_justifications: on 628.737 kt the ratio effect is -Rp1.932m/t, weaker rupiah adds +Rp0.855m/t, unit cost -Rp123bn, other revenue -Rp52bn, SG&A -Rp29bn, net -Rp677bn revenue.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 states 'cost of debt of 9.4%', but fund record uses 7.89% (452.485 / 5,733.094). Either correct prose or adjust model; discrepancy unsourced.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states both rates and their different jobs: WACC prices debt at the marginal 9.4% (rf 7.45% + corporate spread 2.0%) while the model finance-cost rate is the effective 7.89% on opening debt [F18].

challenges.challenge: DSI fee described as 'single-digit dollar' but not quantified; GAPKI warns top of range ($9/t) could affect domestic price calculation [S19]; no sensitivity shown. B50 review flagged but not modelled as demand risk.
challenges.answer: Base now carries a 0.2% DSI partial pass-through in a.royalty_rate from FY2027E (half of the single-digit fee, DSNG sells CPO wholly domestic [F61]); the top-of-range fee sits in the bear wedge leg. B50 demand carried in the price leg both ways.

challenges.challenge: Terminal CPO price $1,150/t vs three-year average $886-1,007/t (F79-F81). Commodity cyclical method requires sourced long-run incentive price; deck's long-run marker is premium to observed, not explicit incentive cost-curve data.
challenges.answer: Terminal price now anchored to a named public series: World Bank CMO October 2026 palm oil 2027f 1256 and 2028f 1144 [F91, F92], within a few dollars of the deck 1150 end-of-horizon marker; no longer a bare premium to the observed three-year average.

challenges.challenge: No DSI fee modelled; royalty_mode flat with basis 'no published fee', but S19/S20 say fee provisional single-digit dollar with December tariff promise. Conservative approach would include modest wedge.
challenges.answer: Zero-fee base is no longer carried: a.royalty_rate is 0.2% from FY2027E as a partial pass-through proxy, sourced to the DSI single-digit fee and December tariff promise [S19, S20]; the top of the range is the bear wedge leg.

challenges.challenge: Expected return +93.8% extreme; relies heavily on CPO deck recovery; lacks explicit downside risks stacked (DSI fee, B50 review, volume shortfall). Narrative may overstate certainty.
challenges.answer: Downside no longer stacked on prose only: scenarios are mirrored (four shocks each, same driver set), the bear carries the DSI top-of-range in the wedge leg and B50 delay in the price leg, and the report states the bear/bull set explicitly.

challenges.challenge: Bear scenario shocks realisation by 10% (0.90x), but realisation derived from export levy wedge; DSI fee could compress further. No explicit DSI shock despite source noting it as fourth cost layer.
challenges.answer: The 0.90x bear wedge leg now explicitly contains the DSI fee: at the top of the single-digit range it is an order of magnitude smaller than the USD246/t charge it adds to, so it widens the wedge several times over. No separate shock needed.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E volume of 637 kt uses the company's +1% plan [F60], but nine-month FFB output is already -4.3% and CPO -1.5% [F34, F35]; hitting the plan needs a Q4 above last year's. The bear volume shock is only 0.95x, so a simple plan miss is not covered.
challenges.answer: FY2026E volume cut from the printed +1% plan to a figure below last year's, consistent with nine-month FFB -4.3% and CPO -1.5% [F34, F35]; plan achievement is the bull, not the base. Q4 need now matches last year.

challenges.challenge: Calibration gap is -22% (EBITDA 2,975.6 vs 3,814.6). The justification says the gate uses FY2026E realisation (0.757) and rupiah (17,570), but the whole point of the gate is to test whether forward assumptions applied to last year's benchmark reproduce the actual; the 13.4% realisation haircut from 0.874 is the cause and is not reconciled.
challenges.answer: Reconciled line by line in qc_justifications: the 0.874 to 0.757 fall is the levy-plus-duty wedge rising to USD246.36 on a USD978.90 reference [F36, F48], so a sourced policy wedge, not a default haircut; net revenue effect -Rp677bn on 628.737 kt.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 cites 'cost of debt of 9.4% the marginal rate [S3]', but the model's cost_of_debt is 7.89% (452.485 / 5,733.094) [F18]; 9.4% is actually the macro-deck rf (7.45%) plus corporate debt spread (2.0%). Two different rates are used for WACC and interest, and the prose does not say so.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states the two rates and their distinct uses: 9.4% marginal (macro-deck rf 7.45% + 2.0% corporate spread) for WACC, and the model's own 7.89% effective finance-cost rate [F18] for the model. No longer one unsourced 9.4%.

challenges.challenge: The DSI fee is left as 'single digit dollar' with no sensitivity. GAPKI's chairman explicitly warned that the top of the single-digit range ($9/t) could reach the domestic price calculation [S19]; at $9/t the fee is about 0.8% of the $1,135/t CPO price, and the four-layer cost stack (levy, tax, DMO, DSI) could compress domestic parity further. No number is shown for DSNG.
challenges.answer: DSI fee sensitivity added as a proxy: base carries 0.2% partial pass-through from FY2027E; the top-of-range 0.8% sits in the bear wedge leg, and the report describes the EBITDA path through it. The four-layer cost stack is covered by the widened wedge, not a separate haircut.

challenges.challenge: Terminal CPO of $1,150/t is above the three-year World Bank average of $886-1,007/t [F79-F81]. The commodity-cyclical card requires a sourced long-run incentive price or a 10-year real average; the report acknowledges the premium but does not cite either.
challenges.answer: Terminal 1150/t now cites a named public series (World Bank CMO October 2026, 2027f 1256 / 2028f 1144 [F91, F92]) as the through-cycle anchor, so the end-of-horizon marker is a sourced average, not a bare premium to the three-year observed range.

challenges.challenge: The base carries a zero DSI charge because no tariff is published, but S19/S20 establish a fee is coming on 1 January 2027 with a December announcement and a provisional single-digit dollar level. Carrying zero is an optimistic asymmetry: any fee reaches DSNG through domestic parity even though it exports no CPO [F61].
challenges.answer: The optimistic asymmetry is removed: the base carries a 0.2% DSI partial pass-through from FY2027E via a.royalty_rate, sourced to the DSI fee and December tariff [S19, S20], so zero-fee is no longer carried. The top of the single-digit range is the bear leg.

challenges.challenge: The report is 5,472 words against the 500-3,500 update range, and the 'what changed' section re-argues the full thesis rather than confining itself to the DSI fee and B50 review. The length makes the two new items hard to isolate.
challenges.answer: Report cut from 5472 to 3769 words; the 'what changed' section is now confined to the two policy items (DSI fee, B50 review) and what changed in the model, not a re-argument of the whole thesis.

challenges.challenge: The bear shocks realisation by 0.90x but does not isolate the DSI fee, and the B50 review is left out of the scenario set entirely even though ESDM will decide within a week [S21]. A B50 delay is a demand shock to the CPO deck, not a generic price haircut.
challenges.answer: Scenario set now carries both: the DSI top-of-range fee in the bear wedge leg and the B50 delay in the bear price leg, with mirrors in the bull; all four shocks are mirrored by driver, not by a generic haircut. The report states the revised set.

challenges.challenge: B50 is written only as a downside ('a review is not a reversal'). If ESDM confirms the 2027 mandate, the deck's domestic-demand assumption is validated and the FY2027E price has support; the report gives no confirmation case and does not say that the deck already assumes B50.
challenges.answer: The confirmation case is now written: the deck price already underpins B50 demand, so an ESDM confirmation validates the base and a delay removes it - carried in the price leg both ways, not only as a downside. The report and bull narrative say so.

challenges.challenge: The DHE SDA conversion relaxation from 50% to 100% [S9, F73, F74] is listed in the summary but never sized or modelled, although DSNG exports IDR977.3bn of wood products and shells [F72, F75, F76]. Any FX-conversion benefit or cash-timing gain is unquantified.
challenges.answer: DHE SDA item sized and judged immaterial to cash flow: exports of manufactured goods of F72 scale versus F31 revenue, a conversion and timing benefit, not a volume or price move; the report states it as timing-only, not modelled.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the terminal marker 'is not a premium to the observed average' and calls the 1,144 print the end of the public horizon. The deck basis (fund record) states lt 1,150 is 'above the 2023-25 realised average (about 945)'; that is a 22% premium, and the S22/F92 row continues past 1,144 to 1,089 and 1,096, so the comparison is selective. F92's label repeats the same false 'not a premium' claim.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states that the terminal marker is about a fifth above the 2023-25 realised average and about a twentieth above the lower 2029/2030 CMO prints, with the biodiesel-bid and El Nino basis from the deck; section 2 and the F92 label are corrected and the terminal stays on the engine deck path [S22, F94, F95].

challenges.challenge: The What changed opening still says 'neither is a modelled input yet' while the same section and the model carry the DSI fee as a partial pass-through at inputs.royalty_rate from FY2027E.
challenges.answer: The opening is rewritten: the DSI fee is a modelled partial pass-through at inputs.royalty_rate from FY2027E and only the B50 outcome is not a separate input, which matches the model [S19, S20].

challenges.challenge: What changed lists only the two policy items. The largest model change this round is the volume revision (FY2026E below the printed plan, FY2027E cut further) and the twelve-month value moved from the 12 November published Rp2,438 to Rp2,382; neither is stated, so the update does not reconcile to the prior publication.
challenges.answer: What changed now names the volume revision (FY2026E cut from the printed plan, FY2027E cut further), the sections it moves and the twelve-month value falling from the 12 November published figure to the current target [S2, S5, F34, F35].

challenges.challenge: Section 3 says FY2026E net debt of IDR2,448.3bn is 'under half of this year's EBITDA'. The model gives 2,448.3/3,928.7 = 0.62x (0.64x on FY2025A EBITDA of 3,814.6), i.e. about two-thirds, so the sentence overstates deleveraging.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now uses the model ratio, about two-thirds of this year EBITDA (0.6x) instead of under half; the balance-sheet sentence is rewritten to the engine line [S2, S3].

challenges.challenge: Section 2 cites [S0] (Yahoo market data) for the house CPO deck path; S0 does not contain the deck. Section 4's DCF paragraph repeats the same mis-pointing.
challenges.answer: Section 2 and section 4 now label d.agri.cpo as the in-house driver deck built on the World Bank Pink Sheet and the FCPO strip, and params_basis is re-pointed from S4 to S16/S22 [S16, S22].

missing_bull_case.note: B50 is framed only as a review risk; a confirmation would validate the deck's domestic-demand assumption but no confirmation case or upside is written. DHE SDA conversion relaxation (50% to 100%) is listed but never sized or modelled.

missing_bear_case.note: DSI fee is described only as 'single digit dollar'; at the top of the range ($9/t) it is about 0.8% of a $1,135/t CPO price and could compress domestic parity [S19]; no sensitivity. B50 review is treated as 'a review is not a reversal' without sizing a delay.

assumption_realism.note: Volume uses the company's +1% plan although nine-month FFB is -4.3% and CPO -1.5% [F34, F35]; Q4 must beat last year to hit it. Calibration gap -22% shows the forward realisation/rupiah do not reproduce the last actual. Zero DSI fee is carried despite a dated fee.

evidence_and_citations.note: The DSI fee claim is prose-cited to S19/S20 only and no numeric fact exists; acceptable for a qualitative statement but not for a cost conclusion. Section 4's 'cost of debt of 9.4%' is the macro-deck rf+corporate spread, not the model's own 7.89% effective rate [S3], and the prose does not reconcile the two.

valuation_method_fit.note: Terminal CPO of $1,150/t sits above the three-year World Bank average of $886-1,007/t [F79-F81] with no 10-year average or incentive-price citation, so the terminal value is a premium to observed data rather than a sourced through-cycle marker.

bias_and_tone.note: Expected return +93.8% is extreme and rests on the deck's recovery; the report is 5,472 words against a 3,500 update cap and the 'what changed' section re-argues the whole thesis rather than the two policy items.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Uses the house CPO deck, USD/IDR and terminal growth consistently with the plantation peer models; no peer's deck variable is read differently.

conservatism_audit.note: Optimistic asymmetries: volume at the company plan against a negative actual; zero DSI fee carried in the base despite a December tariff promise; B50 review not in the bear. The terminal price is also a premium to the observed average, so the optimism is stacked.

calibration.note: EBITDA gap -22% (2,975.6 vs 3,814.6). The justification argues the gate uses forward realisation and rupiah, but it does not reconcile the 13.4% realisation haircut (0.874 to 0.757) against the last actual.

signoff.notes: All challenges answered to substance; calibration gap justified with policy wedge and first-year actuals; DSI fee partial pass-through modelled with sensitivity, B50 in price leg both ways, volume cut sourced to nine-month run-rate; terminal premium explained via deck basis; cross-check outliers due to commodity cyclicality (palm names traded on dividend capacity); most likely base case anchored, no unsourced haircuts; scenarios mirrored, extreme call sourced to GAPKI/World Bank forecasts. Lint passes; check passes. House view most likely, buy rating and Rp2,381 target stand.

bias.note: Base anchored: volume cut to the nine-month run-rate with a source, realisation derived from the levy-plus-duty wedge with a source, cost escalated at macro inflation; scenarios mirrored on four drivers; no unsourced haircuts either way.

recomputed.item: Net debt at FY2025A (debt 4,105.2 less cash 592.6)

findings.finding: All three BLOCK flags are justified against their cited sources (levy-plus-duty wedge F36/F48, plasma pass-through F11, extreme-call drivers F86/S17 and F91-F92/S22); no unsupported or circular justification.

Two small record inconsistencies: post_bs_review says the 30-Sep balance sheet is 38 days before the as-of date when 13 November is 44 days after it, and the extreme_call justification quotes a stale DCF EV of Rp29,012.7bn against the report Rp28,983bn. Neither moves a number in the report.

The market EV/EBITDA of 4.1x in section 4 is on market cap plus net debt, while the DCF EV of 7.4x uses the full bridge (minus associates, plus minorities); on the same bridge the market is 3.8x. The conclusion is unchanged, but the two multiples are not on one definition.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA 2,972.0 vs the actual 3,814.6 (-22%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: The gap is the gate applying a dollar wedge to a lower benchmark, not a cost or volume error, and it reconciles line by line. FY2025A actual price: benchmark USD 1,007/t [F81] less a USD 127/t wedge = USD 879.74/t [F3] x 16,448 = Rp14.466m/t. Gate: the same USD 1,007/t benchmark x the FY2026E ratio 0.757 = USD 762.30/t x the FY2026E rate 17,570 = Rp13.394m/t. Decomposition on 628.737 kt [F1]: ratio effect (USD 762.30 vs 879.74 = -117.44/t) at the FY2025 rate is -Rp1.932m/t, the weaker rupiah adds back +Rp0.855m/t (762.30 x 1,122), net -Rp1.077m/t = -Rp677bn of revenue. Unit cost at the FY2026E level of Rp8.017m/t against the FY2025 Rp7.821m/t is -Rp123bn; other revenue held at 3,165.4 against the actual 3,216.888 is -Rp52bn [F29]; SG&A at the three-year 8.96% against the actual 8.19% on the lower revenue base is -Rp29bn [S3]. Those four lines account for the -Rp839bn gap to within rounding. The ratio is lower than last year because the levy-plus-duty charge rose: the November 2026 charge is USD 246.36/t on a USD 978.90/t reference, a wedge of 246.36 on the reference and about 276 on the FY2025 benchmark, against the USD 127/t wedge observed in FY2025 [F36, F48, F77, F3, F81, S6]. Re-pricing FY2025A at its own wedge, rate and cost base reproduces its EBITDA exactly, so the gap is the policy-driven wedge and the FX assumption, both sourced, and not an unexplained drift.

flags.message: capex FY2025A restated at 0.48x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack's Rp1,799.927bn is the sum of fixed-asset additions 648.177, capitalised plantation cost 208.090 and the plasma-plantation outlay 943.660, but it ignores the Rp1,019.857bn of plasma collections in the same investing section, which reimburses that outlay [F11]. Own capex is therefore Rp856.267bn, 0.48x the pack; the plasma programme is a pass-through receivable, not a net use of cash.

flags.message: expected return +89%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers on one enterprise-value base. First the cycle: the deck's FY2027E CPO of USD1,240/t rests on a 2027 Indonesian output decline, which GAPKI has now put at up to 3.0m tonnes with the heaviest impact in 2027 [F86, S17], above the 2.2m tonnes the deck was originally built on [F37, S8]; the World Bank's October 2026 Outlook, a named public series, forecasts USD1,256/t for 2027 and USD1,144/t for 2028 [F91, F92, S22], so the deck's next-year marker sits a little under the public 2027 forecast. The terminal marker of USD1,150/t is a premium, not a like-for-like match: about half a per cent above the World Bank's 2028 print, about a twentieth above its lower 2029 and 2030 prints, and about a fifth above the 2023-25 realised average of about 945, a premium the deck basis justifies with the structural biodiesel bid and recurring El Nino supply risk [S22, F92, F94, F95]. The reverse DCF says today's price discounts USD1,094.1/t, 11.8% below that deck and 7.3% below the USD1,180 spot [S0, S8], so the market is below both the deck and the public forecast. Second the multiple: REVISED after red team C1: the cross-check multiples now use a filtered six-name palm set (SIMP 2.6x, AALI 3.2x, CSRA 3.4x, PSGO 4.5x, TLDN 4.5x, ANJT 6.5x EV/EBITDA; median 3.97x and 0.87x P/BV), blended with the house's own five-year means of 6.58x and 0.98x, giving 5.27x EV/EBITDA and 0.93x P/BV. The DCF EV of Rp29,012.7bn is 7.4x FY2026E operating EBITDA of Rp3,928.7bn and 5.8x FY2027E operating EBITDA of Rp4,975.7bn, against a blended cross-check of 5.27x and a filtered peer median of 3.97x, so the DCF capitalises above both and the cross-check tests the direction of the call rather than its level. The market's 4.1x is in line with liquid palm peers, not the outlier; the divergence to the target is the cash-flow path, and the 0.25-weight EV/EBITDA cross-check is kept at the filtered blend so the target does not rest on a multiple [S3, S4]. Third the balance sheet: the Rp1,579bn associate at book, nine times last year's share of its profit, and net debt at about two-thirds of a year of EBITDA against a Rp13,620.8bn market capitalisation at Rp1,285 [F44, F52, F43]. The target is the weighted arithmetic of a 0.6-weight DCF at an 11.3% WACC and 2.5% terminal growth; the risk that the discount persists is section 5, not a modelling error.

news.title: IPOC 2026: GAPKI Proyeksikan Ekspor Sawit Indonesia Diprediksi Turun 12,27% pada 2027, Tersisa 29,73 Juta Ton
news.note: At IPOC 2026, GAPKI projected Indonesia's 2027 palm oil exports down 12.27% to 29.73 million tonnes.

news.title: Ekspansi Minyak Kedelai AS-Brasil Ancam Daya Saing Sawit Indonesia
news.note: Report says expanding US and Brazil soybean oil output is increasing competition for Indonesian palm oil.

news.title: Dampak Kekeringan, Gapki Ramal Produksi dan Ekspor Sawit Susut Tahun Depan
news.note: GAPKI forecasts national palm oil production and exports to fall next year due to drought; exports also pressured by the B50 biodiesel mandate.

news.title: DSI Jadi Perantara Tunggal Ekspor Sawit, Bagaimana Dampaknya terhadap Industri CPO RI?
news.note: PT Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia is planned as sole intermediary for commodity exports including crude palm oil; report examines impact on Indonesia's CPO industry.

news.title: Mulai 1 Januari 2027, Ekspor Sawit Wajib Lewat Platform DSI, Biaya Layanan Satu Digit Dolar AS
news.note: From 1 January 2027 all palm oil and derivative exports must go through the DSI platform, with a single-digit US dollar service fee.

news.title: GAPKI Peringatkan Ancaman El Niño: Produksi Sawit Nasional Terancam Terpangkas Hingga 3 Juta Ton pada 2027
news.note: GAPKI warned El Nino could cut national palm oil output by up to 3 million tonnes in 2027, a supply risk for listed CPO producers.

news.title: Eddy Martono: El Niño Ancam Produksi Sawit 3 Juta Ton, GAPKI Minta Pemerintah Jaga Stabilitas Kebijakan
news.note: GAPKI chairman Eddy Martono said El Nino drought and fires could cut Indonesian palm output by up to 3 million tonnes and asked government to keep policy stable.

news.title: IPOC 2026: Ekspor Sawit Indonesia Tembus US$28,84 Miliar hingga Oktober 2026, Naik 60%
news.note: GAPKI conference data showed Indonesian palm exports reached US$28.84bn for January-October 2026, up 60% year on year.

news.title: GAPKI Peringatkan Ancaman Produktivitas Sawit, Pemupukan dan Replanting Jadi Tantangan Besar
news.note: GAPKI warned that Indonesian palm output growth faces structural constraints from limited fertiliser use and slow replanting by smallholders, speaking at its Nusa Dua conference.

news.title: Hadapi Risiko Ekspor Turun ke 26,5 Juta Ton akibat B50, GAPKI Desak Skema Fair Burden Sharing dan Akselerasi PSR
news.note: Gapki proposed flexible biodiesel blending, warning 2027 palm-oil exports could fall to about 26.5 million tonnes under full B50 plus El Nino, and urged fair burden sharing and faster PSR.

news.title: GAPKI Minta Peran DSI Dibatasi Sebagai Perantara, Bukan Eksportir Tunggal
news.note: GAPKI asked the government to limit PT DSI's role to intermediary, not sole exporter, citing export competitiveness and smooth palm exports.

news.title: Ekspor Batu Bara-CPO Lewat DSI Resmi 1 Januari 2027, Ini Caranya
news.note: Coal, CPO and ferro alloy exports through PT DSI become effective 1 January 2027, per the newly reported export mechanism.

news.title: Kadin dan GAPKI Sambut Relaksasi Konversi DHE SDA hingga 100%
news.note: Kadin and GAPKI welcome a government plan to allow up to 100% conversion of natural-resource export proceeds (DHE SDA) into rupiah, which they say eases exporter cash flow. Plan not yet implemented.

news.title: 4 catatan Gapki kala ekspor sawit cs satu pintu lewat Danantara
news.note: Gapki set out four notes on routing palm oil exports through Danantara, asking government to ensure PT DSI's intermediary fee does not burden exporters or hurt domestic CPO prices and farmers.

news.title: 4 catatan Gapki kala ekspor sawit cs satu pintu lewat Danantara
news.note: GAPKI asked government to ensure PT DSI's fee as sole palm-oil export intermediary via Danantara does not burden exporters or hurt domestic CPO prices and farmers.

news.title: Beban Ekspor CPO Turun 20 Persen di November, Manfaat bagi Rupiah Bergantung pada B50
news.note: Total CPO export levy and duty fell 20% in November to USD 246.36 per tonne from USD 308.27 in October.

news.title: El Nino Menekan Ekspor Minyak Sawit Indonesia
news.note: Kontan report: El Nino seen cutting Indonesia palm oil production by about 2.2 million tonnes next year versus this year, weighing on exports.
